conflicts.fact: Which nitrogenous waste marine fish excrete, and what fish excrete in general
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says marine fish and mammals make urea and that marine fish excrete very little concentrated urine, with urea/TMAO only in cartilaginous fish. Lesson 7 says freshwater fish make ammonia and mammals make urea, and the sequence never separates marine bony fish from cartilaginous fish. This is an internal oversimplification rather than a clear contradiction, but Lesson 1 'marine fish make urea' conflicts with its own detail that this applies only to cartilaginous fish.

conflicts.fact: Group size and number of groups for the same class
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 uses groups of 4-6, Lesson 2 groups of 4-5 (about 10 groups), Lesson 3 groups of 6-8, and Lessons 4-7 groups of 5-6. Group sizes vary across the sequence.

conflicts.fact: Skin excretion function and what the 'dog-like mammal' loses heat by; sweat vs panting
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 frames the question around a dog-like mammal such as a human sweating and says sweat helps animals lose heat. Lesson 4's DQB asks 'If sweat cools us, why do dogs pant instead?' Lesson 6 groups dogs with sweating endotherms ('sweat glands, panting') and lists sweating as a dog response. The sequence is inconsistent on whether dogs sweat.

Lesson 2 says the cortex contains many nephrons where blood is filtered and nephrons are packed in the cortex and medulla; and says a goat kidney has about a million nephrons. Lesson 3 says 'millions of nephrons'. Minor numeric wording difference.

conflicts.fact: Place/time and sequencing of ADH/urea in earlier lesson
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 teacher says 'Last lesson we followed urea through the nephron', while Lesson 3 is the nephron lesson and Lesson 5 says 'Take out your model from last lesson' regarding Lesson 4 content. Lesson 3 ends asking what other organs help, consistent; but Lesson 3 says 'Yesterday we saw that the kidney has millions of nephrons' fine. Lesson 5 DQB lists dog/lizard as unanswered while Lesson 4 DQB already raises temperature questions.
